result.summary: The hymn praises Earth as the eldest being and mother of all, who feeds every creature and grants or withholds the means of life. It describes the prosperity of those she honours and ends with a greeting and a request for a reward for the song.

scenes.title: Hymn to Earth
scenes.summary: The singer praises Earth as nourisher of all creatures and giver of prosperity, then greets her and asks for a reward.

characters.name: Earth
characters.description: eldest of all beings, mother of all, wife of starry Heaven

alias_notes.explanation: A title addressed to Earth in the closing greeting.

notable_quotes.reason: Opening line states Earth's primacy as eldest being and mother of all.

analysis.text: Earth is honoured as the source of all life and fertility, with human prosperity depending on her favour.
Like other Homeric Hymns, it works as a short prelude to a performance, ending with a request for reward and a transition to another song.

legacy.text: The hymn's image of Earth as universal mother belongs to a long tradition of earth-goddess worship, later echoed in the idea of Mother Earth.

fun_facts.text: The hymn is short, only 19 lines, and the lines are marked in the translation as 1-16 and 17-19.

language_notes.text: "Well-founded" renders a traditional epithet meaning firmly set or solid, stressing Earth's stability as the base of the world.
"Fed of her store" means nourished from her supplies; "of" here has the older sense "by" or "from".
"Blessed in their children" means made fortunate through having children; fertility of people and crops both depend on Earth.
"Wife of starry Heaven" refers to Earth's union with Heaven (Uranus), the old Greek myth of the first divine couple.
"I will remember you and another song" is a formula closing a hymn and moving on to the next song.

context_notes.text: Earth (Gaia) was worshipped as the primeval goddess, born at the start of the world and ancestor of gods and mortals.
Hymn singers commonly ask the god for a reward, here prosperity, in return for the praise just given.

literary_notes.text: The singer shifts from speaking about Earth to addressing her directly as "you, O queen," creating the intimacy of prayer.
Dancing girls in flower-laden bands over soft meadows give a vivid picture of the joy and abundance Earth grants.
